about: Settings of the library-motion tool (tools/anim/README.md). The frames are drawn 1:1 at the 64 px tile: today's 16 px tile shown at 4x, the scale the cut-out demo draws at. The paces are read from content/core/params.json by these keys. The limits are what `pnpm anim check` fails on.

forager.about: The forager, the man (character-forager-m.glb), as the 3D game uses him (Mixamo bone names), lit and snapped to his ramps.
forager.credit: Forager, generated with Meshy (meshy.ai), CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (game/public3d/models/README.md); modified: posed with library motion and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

mage.about: The mage of the character experiments: a long dark robe. Mixamo bone names, the forager's scale and camera. Its skeleton was transferred from the warrior, not fitted to its body (the mesh is not standing on the ground plane): trial 3 found the robe torn and the props hidden; fit it as the six people were (game/tools/blender/person_rig.py) before its sheets are used.

rig.about: A 19-bone body rig (.blend, rigid parts on bones: hips, spine, neck, head, upper_arm/forearm/hand/tool and thigh/shin/foot per side), path from ANIM_RIG_BLEND. Heights are modelled stretched by 1/cos 30 for the 30 degree camera it was drawn for; it takes the 50 degree camera like every target, and the stretch is checked again when it is rendered at 50 (its .blend is not in the repo).

elf-m.about: The elf, the man (round 4 E4-A, version 3): the Universal Base Characters body thinned at the bones and lengthened on the shared rig, in the ranger outfit under a pastel green open hooded cloak (green since 30.10; sky blue at the pick) (tools/anim/races/elf.json).
elf-m.credit: Elf, built from Quaternius Universal Base Characters and Modular Character Outfits - Fantasy (CC0 1.0); the cloak is own geometry; posed with Quaternius Universal Animation Library motion (CC0 1.0) and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

elf-f.about: The elf, the woman (round 4 E4-A, version 3): as the man, in the female base body and outfit, long hair.

skeleton.about: The skeleton (round 2 B): the thin white Brodin skeleton, cut into bone pieces and fitted piece by piece onto the shared rig (tools/anim/races/skeleton.json), 81 percent of the human's height.
skeleton.credit: Skeleton by Alexander Brodin (https://poly.pizza/m/frU5VxsCGZJ), CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/); modified: cut into bone pieces, each fitted to a bone of the Quaternius Universal Base Characters skeleton, posed with Quaternius Universal Animation Library motion (CC0 1.0) and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

wolf.about: The wolf, dark grey (character-wolf-grim.glb): a four-legged body that carries its own Idle, Walk and Run, so nothing is retargeted ('native'). The feet are the tails of the last bone of each leg. The camera is the forager's; the scale makes the wolf about 0.9 m at the ears.
wolf.credit: Wolf, generated with Meshy (meshy.ai), CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; modified: the emission input removed (it repeated the colour map) and the colour map cut from 2048 to 1024 px; scaled to 0.9 m at the ears; Meshy's walk renamed Walk; Run made from the walk and Idle made from the standing pose in Blender (game/tools/blender/quad_pass.py); posed with its own actions and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

deer.about: The roe deer (animal-deer.glb): a four-legged body that carries its own Idle, Walk, Run, Alert, Graze and Lie, so nothing is retargeted ('native'). The feet are the tails of the hoof bones. The camera is the forager's; the scale makes the deer about 0.75 m at the withers.
deer.credit: Deer Female by CDmir (collaborator: TinyWorlds), OpenGameArt, CC0, https://opengameart.org/content/deer-female; modified: the camera, the lamps and the ground plane removed; the body, head and eye meshes joined; the Blender Internal materials rebuilt as Principled BSDFs on the packed colour maps, the eye given a plain dark material and the tip of the muzzle the same dark material (a nose); the colour maps re-encoded as JPEG (quality 90); the body centred over the origin and scaled to 0.75 m at the withers with the scale baked into the bones, and a tip bone under each hoof (the renderer reads a foot from its bone's tail); the ears carried spread outward in every action; Idle, Graze (Eat held at its lowest with a small chew and an ear flick) and Lie (the last pose of the second Die, the legs drawn in, held still) resampled from the file's actions; Walk (a calm four-beat pace), Run (a four-beat rotary gallop) and Alert (from the standing pose: the head carried high and a slow look to each side) keyed in Blender (game/tools/blender/deer_pass.py); the other actions dropped; posed with its own actions and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

hart.about: The white hart (animal-hart.glb): the roe deer's body and actions in a second look, the colour map washed to an even silver white, the ears smaller, the neck thicker and a pair of branched antlers skinned to the head, about 1.1 m at the withers. The tool recolours a body only through its ramps, so the pale look is a second glb from the same pass (deer_pass.py --look hart), drawn in pale ramps.
hart.credit: Deer Female by CDmir (collaborator: TinyWorlds), OpenGameArt, CC0, https://opengameart.org/content/deer-female; modified: the camera, the lamps and the ground plane removed; the body, head and eye meshes joined; the Blender Internal materials rebuilt as Principled BSDFs on the packed colour maps, the eye given a plain dark material and the tip of the muzzle the same dark material (a nose); the colour maps re-encoded as JPEG (quality 90); the body centred over the origin and scaled to 1.1 m at the withers with the scale baked into the bones, and a tip bone under each hoof (the renderer reads a foot from its bone's tail); the colour maps washed to an even silver white; the ears made smaller and the neck thicker (the bind-pose mesh moved along its own bone weights); a pair of branched antlers modelled and skinned to the head; the ears carried spread outward in every action; Idle, Graze (Eat held at its lowest with a small chew and an ear flick) and Lie (the last pose of the second Die, the legs drawn in, held still) resampled from the file's actions; Walk (a calm four-beat pace), Run (a four-beat rotary gallop) and Alert (from the standing pose: the head carried high and a slow look to each side) keyed in Blender (game/tools/blender/deer_pass.py); the other actions dropped; posed with its own actions and rendered to pixels by tools/anim
